content: Vectorized numpy haversine over array columns vs .apply(lambda row: haversine(...), axis=1) is roughly 5-10x+ faster at ~10k rows and the gap widens supralinearly with size (100x+ at higher N); apply() with a Python-level function per row defeats pandas' columnar/vectorized execution model entirely. Standard optimization: pull lat/lon columns to numpy arrays (.values / .to_numpy()) and compute with vectorized trig (np.sin/cos/arctan2) once.
